title: Truckers and merchant customers protest Cementis Comores price increase
reason: The reported grievance is solely a private supplier pricing decision; the source documents no demand to the Comorian state or public policy. The number of people is also unreported, so a qualifying crowd of at least 50 is not established.
notes: La Gazette reports truckers queuing with engines off at a Moroni cement outlet and protesting the increase from 70,000 to 79,000 KMF per tonne, effective 1 January. Its 5 January story says the trucks were lined at the outlet on “this Monday,” calendar-anchored to 3 January, and says the grievance remained strong through Tuesday 4 January; it does not establish the physical gathering end. Do not treat trucks as a participant count. A customer collective had unsuccessfully attempted negotiation with the company. The indexed print issue S002 is only search evidence and is not independent corroboration. First-pass screening exclusion; both the content judgment and episode/date notes remain provisional pending independent review. The actual article body was returned and read, while a separate addendum records a later-identified physical-ledger path omission in the pre-body scope map; no retrospective clearance is claimed.
